flowTitle.text: Building travel-sync from scratch, in the order a builder works: start blank, trigger, connections, record types, then each step

dataTitle.text: The Add menu, and a free-form variant of travel-sync

freeformNote.text: Free-form is the third flow block. It is free only within the order its data sets: a step can run once its inputs exist. The block draws that order, the builder adds rules the planner can't skip (Before finishing), and the planner chooses the rest: follow-up searches, what to verify, when to stop. Only Ask and Built-in steps go inside. Modeled on travel-sync's --mode free.

invoiceTitle.text: Pressure test: invoice-check, a second agent built around a Free-form block

invoiceNote.text: What the second example forced into the design: (1) a record can come from more than one step (PO number from the invoice or from vendor emails); (2) inputs can be optional (no receipts for services); (3) the block needs named outcomes, and finishing rules can depend on the outcome; (4) safety checks must be finishing rules, because a fooled planner's risk is skipping steps, not running them; (5) Built-in steps should re-run by themselves when inputs change; (6) tests need one sample per outcome, not one happy path.

homeNote.text: The two newest travel-sync runs are real: the 13:39 run on sample data (times, costs, tokens and the planner's reasons come from its Conductor event log) and the 13:36 run that failed because Claude Opus 5.5 can't return structured output through Conductor.
